analysis: All 98 critical rules (m <= 5, J <= 4, b_j <= 4, gcd-1 support) have a simple eigenvalue 1 and all other eigenvalues of modulus < 1 (max 0.949); every start beyond the largest terminating one (<= 124) is certified non-terminating - as Theorem 9 predicts.
assumptions: all critical rules with m <= 5, J <= 4, b_j <= 4 and gcd of support 1 (b_J > 0)
falsification: A rule with an eigenvalue of modulus >= 1 other than the simple eigenvalue 1, or a terminating start after the first certified one beyond a stable tail.

hypothesis: T-C02-12: if sum b = m and gcd{j : b_j > 0} = 1, the window map's linearisation has the simple eigenvalue 1 (eigenvector T = tail sums) and all other eigenvalues of modulus < 1; consequently every unary start n >= n0 reaches a window dominating T and never terminates.
methodology: For each rule: eigenvalues of the J x J linear map (A x)_i = x_(i+1) + (b_i/m) x_1; sweep every start up to 2000 with periodic/pumping certificates; record the largest terminating start n0 - 1 and check that every larger start has a certificate.
question: Is non-termination of critical rules (sum b = m) a property of all large starts, as a spectral argument predicts?

summary: 98 critical rules with gcd-1 support (m <= 5, J <= 4): spectral violations 0
